head_commit.message:
Heilbronn: up to 300 digits per integer of a bound (40 on every other problem)

Lead, 2026-11-03 (verifier #105, darkhipo's follow-up): a Heilbronn saving with a full proof can be very small:
the comparator exponent 1/(100000 K), K = T^2 + 1, has a 237-digit denominator, and the smallest positive bound with
40 digits per integer (1/(10^40 - 1)) is far larger, so rounding down to 40 digits gives the refused 0.

- submissions.py: BOUND_DIGITS = {heilbronn-triangle: 300}; bound_digits(problem) is 40 for every other problem.
  validate_submission checks the problem first, then the bound with its limit; the error names the limit and the
  problem. exact_value takes the limit, and other_record passes the row's limit, so a Lean Verified saving with a
  237-digit denominator gates the row (with 40 it was dropped and the row fell back to the range end). The code
  comment names the 40-digit limit as the Lead decision of 2026-10-21 (issue #35), not a Nil ruling.
- README and docs/targets.md state the limits. The issue form is unchanged.
- Tests: η = 1/(100000 K) parses and gives the target Bound ((1 : ℚ) / <237 digits>); 300 digits pass and 301
  do not on Heilbronn; 40 pass and 41 do not on Catalan; a 237-digit Lean Verified value gates the row.
  248 OK, also with BOS_SPLIT=true.

The site half (normalize with the same per-problem limit) must be on the site's main branch before this commit is
pushed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
